Hi Alicia / Roberto — great conversation this morning. Thanks for walking us through the payment flows and the anomalous chargeback examples — super helpful. Per the call, I wanted to summarize recommended next steps and the contingency playbook we discussed for any model-quality regressions after version changes.

Quick summary:
- Recommended candidate models: Redwood-llama-13b-qa (baseline) and Redwood-opt-6.7b-quant (cost-optimized).
- Deliverables we attached/linked: benchmark CSV (key metrics on your sample corpus), the prompt set we used, and an initial mutual action plan (MAP).
- Contingency: we can pin a snapshotable model variant for production traffic within 2 hours and we maintain a rollback playbook that re-routes traffic to the pinned variant while we triage.

Action items / asks from NimbusPay:
1) Confirm the primary inference SLA requirement (p95 latency target and max acceptable PR% for false positives).
2) Share a small (1-2k) redacted sample of real queries for the eval run (secure upload link in MAP).
3) Approval to run a short canary (2% traffic) using Redwood-llama-13b-qa this week — Karthik can run the bench and post results.

Attachments: nimbus-benchmarks-20260914.csv, nimbus-prompt-set-v1.txt
Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-nimbus-benchmarks, HubSpot:HS-546221

If that aligns, we’ll schedule the canary and Karthik will share the evaluation artifact and a diff checklist we use to decide whether to pin/rollback.

Thanks —

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear note. A couple of clarifying points before we sign off:

1) On the pin/rollback SLA — in our pilot last quarter we saw a model update that changed tokenization and led to a ~6% regression in our fraud recall on certain merchant types. How fast can you pin and how do you guarantee the pinned snapshot will be identical to the version we test?
2) For the canary, would Redwood be able to generate a per-request trace (token-level diff + output hash) so our fraud team can quickly validate there’s no unexpected semantic shift?

Also copying procurement to start the paperwork: procurement@nimbuspay.com

Appreciate it — Alicia

On Wed, 15 Sep 2026 at 10:01, Alicia Gomez <alicia@nimbuspay.com> wrote:
> 1) On the pin/rollback SLA — in our pilot last quarter we saw a model update that changed tokenization and led to a ~6% regression in our fraud recall on certain merchant types. How fast can you pin and how do you guarantee the pinned snapshot will be identical to the version we test?
> 2) For the canary, would Redwood be able to generate a per-request trace (token-level diff + output hash) so our fraud team can quickly validate there’s no unexpected semantic shift?

Hi Alicia — quick answers:
- Pinning: we snapshot the exact model artifact (commit + quantization metadata + kernel selection table) and store it as an immutable variant. For Hosted customers we can create that pinned variant and route traffic to it in under 2 hours for emergency pins; for Dedicated/Private we provide the same artifact and a pinning API (PATCH /models/:id/pin) that your infra can call — the variant is byte-for-byte identical to the snapshot used for evaluation.
- Traceability: yes — for canaries we emit an optional per-request analysis bundle that includes: input, canonicalized tokenization, output hash (SHA256), model variant id, and a simple token-diff visualization. We can redact tokens if needed for PII. We’ll include a sample trace for a few requests in the bench artifact.

Recommended baseline plan (what I’ll run once we have your sample):
1) Run the bench on the 1-2k sample with Redwood-llama-13b-qa and opt-6.7b-quant. I’ll provide p95 latency, token cost, recall/precision on your golden labels, and a per-case diff report.
2) If the diff report shows >3% drop in recall for a merchant cohort, we flag for immediate pin and initiate rollback routing while we triage.
3) Canary: 2% traffic for 24 hrs with per-request traces to your fraud team.

Attachments: I exported the initial bench CSV with per-case diffs (attached) and the prompt set used — see nimbus-benchmarks-20260914.csv, nimbus-prompt-set-v1.txt.

If that works I’ll schedule the bench for Thursday morning and post a short summary.

— Karthik

- Defined acceptance criteria tied to the evaluation artifacts (bench CSV + per-request trace);
- A credits-based remedy if a regression above an agreed threshold is observed and we fail to meet the containment SLA.
